failure: Real documents with headed long-prose code fences lost hundreds of source lines, gained empty pages, or parked blocks in hidden overflow columns, while the app reported success. Paged.js 0.4.3 marks every inline-styled element data-undisplayed, so a heading's break-after: avoid skipped its Shiki pre and landed on the next heading; when that heading overflowed on a page that began inside the code block, Paged.js backed up to the block start and stopped with 'Layout repeated'. preview() still resolved. Tier 3 measured heights outside the .doc styling context (906px recorded for a block needing over 971px), so over-tall blocks stayed break-inside: avoid. Separately, every re-render ran under a preview zoom below 1, where Paged.js adds an unscaled column gap to scaled rects and leaves overflowing blocks in hidden overflow columns.
workaround: None needed: fixed at the root. A handler filter hook clears the bogus mark before break propagation; layout runs at zoom 1; heights are measured in context; over-tall code/table/quote/callout blocks are marked splittable (Tier 4); media is capped to the page; every run is audited and recovered or refused (fatal state, export ineligible).
future_fix: Closed by tests/e2e/pagination-completeness.spec.ts (long-prose-fences fixture, forced stall, unrecoverable stall). Recheck restoreDisplayedElements if Paged.js is upgraded past 0.4.3.
